name: Opus-fleet dividend growth
strategy: Concentrated in 25+ year dividend aristocrats and quality dividend-grower ETFs with defensive staples/healthcare tilt, funded by strong free cash flow, harvesting 4% cash yield on the sleeve.

positions.thesis: Core anchor, upsized from 18% to 33%. Schwab US Dividend Equity ETF is the single purest instrument for this mandate: 103 quality-screened dividend growers with 10-year streaks, 3.10% yield, a 0.06% fee that is 6x cheaper than NOBL, and a 28.94% trailing 1yr total return. It just crossed $100B AUM. With VIX at 20.66 and semis unwinding, the quality-income factor is precisely what should work, and because this is a diversified basket a one-third weight adds conviction without adding single-name or earnings-date risk. Deep 12% stop as portfolio-level protection only.

Largest single name, nearly doubled from 7%. 62-year Dividend King that reported Jul 28 with 5% volume growth, 6% organic revenue, double-digit EPS growth and RAISED FY26 guidance — the earnings binary is already resolved in my favour. UBS and Jefferies both moved to $104 against $89.08, roughly 17% upside, and the FIFA World Cup sponsorship is driving record engagement. It closed +0.92% on a day the S&P fell 1.52%, which is exactly the defensive-with-momentum behaviour the mandate wants.

Upsized from 5%. 53-year raiser that beat on Jul 16 with adj EPS $1.31 versus $1.28 and RAISED FY26 guidance to $5.45-5.60. FDA nod to commercialize Freenome's blood-based colorectal screening opens a large new diagnostics market. Closed green on a broadly red tape. Diversified medtech/diagnostics cash flow is the defensive healthcare ballast my mandate calls for, and unlike ABBV its quarter is already banked.

New position. 38-year dividend raiser yielding 3.71% — the highest-quality yield in the book — at just 11.1x forward earnings, with $215 consensus (+12%) and BofA at $227. Energy was the only resilient sector on Jul 29 (+2.28% for CVX against a -1.52% S&P) on elevated crude and strong refining margins. Sized alongside a trimmed XOM so my two Jul 31 energy prints together stay at 15% rather than dominating the book.

Held at 8%. 53-year raise streak via Abbott heritage, 2.63% yield, 17.8x forward earnings, with Barclays and BMO moving to $300 and Wells to $295 on European Commission approvals for Rinvoq in severe alopecia areata and vitiligo. Not upsized because consensus sits at $268.68 versus $263.30 and it reports Jul 31 — the upside is analyst-target-driven and the print is a genuine coin flip, so a 10% stop is attached rather than more size.

Trimmed from 7% held flat but reweighted behind CVX. 40+ year raiser with enormous free cash flow, up 2.42% on a sharply down tape as Big Oil profits surge on geopolitical supply concerns. Kept rather than added to because BofA just moved it to Neutral, its 2.63% yield trails Chevron's 3.71%, and it shares a Jul 31 earnings date with CVX — I want energy exposure, not a doubled-up single-day event.

Trimmed from 8%. The Jul 29 print beat on core EPS at $1.43 but missed revenue at $21.2B versus $21.38B, guided FY27 to only 1-3% organic growth, and drew an HSBC downgrade to Hold at $142; management explicitly flagged consumers shifting to smaller packs and promotions. I keep a reduced core because it remains a 68-year raiser at a 2.98% yield and 22x with a $161.78 Buy consensus, but the growth impulse has clearly weakened. Wide 12% stop so ballast is not shaken out by noise.

Trimmed from 8%. FY26 EPS guidance cut to $10.86-11.01 from $11.50-11.65, EPS down 7.6%, and a $5.5B settlement covering roughly 76,000 talc suits, with the stock down 1.63% after hours and consensus offering only 1.9% upside. Retained at reduced size because it is a 63-year Dividend King with an AAA-caliber balance sheet and the OTTAVA robotic surgery authorization is a real option — this is low-beta ballast, just less of it. Wide 12% stop.

Trimmed from 5%. The Jul 29 quarter was genuinely strong — 7% revenue growth, 17% adjusted EPS growth, FY27 guided to 5-6% revenue and 9-11% EPS — and it remains a 50-year aristocrat with asset-light payroll economics and float income that benefits from high short rates. Trimmed rather than added because the stock jumped 3.48% straight through the $270 analyst consensus and 18 analysts sit at Hold, leaving no valuation headroom.

Halved from 6%. A 48-year raiser with durable franchise-model free cash flow, but it trades at $271.52 near its 52-week low of $260.96 against a $341.75 high, with UBS, BTIG and Evercore all cutting targets. Kept at half size as a depressed-price call option on the Aug 3 print and the 'greater than NEXT' automation strategy, with a tight 8% stop because I will not ride it further down.

reassessment_note: Unrestricted-retail resize (2026-07-30, free internet + no sizing caps): The book is working (+2.76% NAV, -0.45% max drawdown) but three positions deteriorated on hard news in the last 48 hours and two improved on beat-and-raise quarters, so I am resizing rather than rebuilding. CUTS: CAT to zero — a 31-year streak does not save a 0.83%-yielding AI-capex cyclical that fell 6.91% in a session on a Baird downgrade plus the New York data-center construction moratorium; it was the least mandate-true line I owned and the news confirmed it. LOW to zero — consumer discretionary near its 52-week low while P&G's own management describes consumers downtrading to smaller packs and promotions; that is not defensive cash flow. NOBL to zero — 0.35% fee and +15.0% trailing 1yr versus SCHD's 0.06% and +28.9%, and once I hold nine aristocrats directly its equal-weight basket is redundant. TRIMS: PG 8 to 6 on the revenue miss, the 1-3% FY27 organic guide and the HSBC downgrade; JNJ 8 to 5 on the guidance cut to $10.86-11.01 and the $5.5B talc settlement, with only 1.9% to consensus; ADP 5 to 4 because a 17% EPS-growth quarter is excellent but the stock popped 3.48% straight through the $270 consensus target; MCD 6 to 3, half size into an Aug 3 print at a depressed price. ADDS: SCHD 18 to 33 — this is where my genuine conviction sits, and the new freedom lets me express it. It is the single cleanest instrument for this exact mandate at a 0.06% fee, 3.10% yield and 28.94% trailing return, and because it is a 103-stock quality basket a 33% weight carries almost no idiosyncratic or earnings-event risk; this is concentration into diversification, not variance for its own sake. KO 7 to 13, my largest single name, on a Jul 28 beat with 5% volume and 6% organic growth, RAISED FY guidance, a World Cup engagement tailwind and fresh $104 targets from UBS and Jefferies against $89.08. New CVX at 8% — a 38-year raiser yielding 3.71% at 11x forward earnings with $215 consensus, a better dividend-growth expression of the strongest sector than XOM alone. ABT 5 to 9 on the beat-and-raise and its habit of closing green on red days. ABBV held at 8 and XOM trimmed 7 into their Jul 31 prints, deliberately sized so that one shared earnings date does not dominate the book. Net effect: gross exposure unchanged at 96% with the mandated 4% cash sleeve earning 4% APY, but the staples/healthcare/quality-income core is denser, the cyclical and consumer-discretionary drift is gone, and turnover is cheap at roughly 2bps per side.
novelty: I manage no Round-2 book in this experiment — Round 3 is my only account — so the same-direction overlap test has no counterparty book to measure against; independently, this book turns over meaningfully from its own prior version, retiring CAT, LOW and NOBL outright (18 points of gross weight), cutting PG, JNJ, ADP and MCD by a further 8 points, introducing CVX as a new line, and shifting the center of gravity from a twelve-line spread into a SCHD-and-KO-anchored core.
research_notes:
Market tape (Jul 29 close): S&P 500 7,316.15 (-1.52%), Dow 51,594 (-2.19%), Nasdaq 24,443 (-1.74%), VIX +13.45% to 20.66, gold +1.15% to $4,144. Semis/tech led the decline (ARM -8.1%, LRCX -6.4%, QCOM -4.4%); energy was the lone resilient sector (XLE +1.88% on the day). This is a risk-off quality rotation, which is the tape my mandate is built for.

Name-level research:
- SCHD $33.83, 3.10% yield, 0.06% fee, 103 holdings, just crossed $100B AUM, +28.94% trailing 1yr total return. Cheapest and best-performing pure expression of quality dividend growth; no single-name earnings binary.
- NOBL $58.21, 2.00% yield, 0.35% fee, +15.01% trailing 1yr, beta 0.76. Strictly dominated by SCHD on fee and return; redundant diversification once I hold 9 aristocrats directly.
- KO $89.08 (+0.92% on a -1.5% tape), 2.38% yield. Q2 reported Jul 28: 5% volume growth, 6% organic revenue, double-digit EPS growth, FY26 guidance RAISED. UBS and Jefferies both to $104 (~17% upside). World Cup/FIFA sponsorship driving engagement. Up ~26% YTD. Best fundamental momentum on mandate.
- CVX $191.86 (+2.28%), 3.71% yield, forward P/E 11.1, 38-year raise streak, consensus $215 (+12%), BofA to $227. Earnings Jul 31. Highest-quality yield available to me.
- XOM $156.75 (+2.42%), 2.63% yield, earnings Jul 31, consensus $167 (+6.7%). BofA downgraded to Neutral. "Big Oil profits soaring" on elevated crude and strong refining margins.
- ABT $108.00 (+0.68% on a red day), 2.33% yield. Q2 Jul 16: adj EPS $1.31 vs $1.28 est, FY26 guidance RAISED to $5.45-5.60. FDA nod for Freenome blood-based CRC screening. Beat-and-raise defensive healthcare.
- ABBV $263.30, 2.63% yield, forward P/E 17.8, earnings Jul 31. Barclays/BMO to $300, Wells to $295. EC approvals for Rinvoq in alopecia areata and vitiligo. Near 52wk high ($267.47) but consensus target only $268.68 — upside is analyst-target-driven, so binary into earnings.
- PG $146.10 (-1.87%). Reported Jul 29: core EPS $1.43 beat $1.41 but revenue $21.2B MISSED $21.38B; soft FY27 guide of 1-3% organic; HSBC downgrade to Hold, $142 target; management flagged consumers trading down to smaller packs and promotions. Fundamentals deteriorating.
- JNJ $265.53, -1.63% after hours. Cut FY26 EPS view to $10.86-11.01 from $11.50-11.65; $5.5B settlement of ~76,000 talc suits; EPS -7.6%. Offset by OTTAVA robotic surgery FDA authorization. Consensus target $270.59 = only 1.9% upside.
- ADP $273.37 (+3.48%). Q4 reported Jul 29: 7% revenue growth, 17% adj EPS growth, FY27 guide 5-6% revenue / 9-11% EPS. But 18 analysts at Hold with a $270 target — BELOW the post-pop price. Good business, no headroom.
- CAT $782.71, -6.91% in one session. Baird downgrade to Hold on regulatory cost risk; New York data-center construction moratorium hits its AI-power-equipment business. Earnings Aug 4. Yield only 0.83% — it had drifted into being an AI-capex cyclical rather than a dividend grower. Off-mandate.
- LOW $215.68, near 52wk low of $199.40 vs high $293.06, earnings Aug 19. Home improvement into a consumer that PG just described as trading down.
- MCD $271.52, near 52wk low $260.96 vs high $341.75. UBS, BTIG and Evercore all cut targets. Earnings Aug 3.
- PEP $143.50, 4.13% yield but -16% YTD, broad analyst downgrades, North America snacks weakness. High yield masking a broken story — declined; my mandate wants dividend GROWTH quality, not a falling knife.
- VIG 1.50% yield, top holdings AVGO/AAPL/LLY — effectively a tech-quality fund, wrong exposure into a semis unwind. Declined.
